description: utopia-php/bus: a synchronous in-process event bus with typed events, listeners with injected dependencies, and failures recorded on the current span.

bus.dispatch.doc: A Bus with a resolver (`suffix` (default): name.':resolved'; `none`: no resolver; {fail: [names]}: throws Exception('cannot resolve <name>') for those, else the name), the listeners subscribed in order (classes clock and mailer handle Deployed, refunds Cancelled, audit all three, twice Created twice; each with `injections` and a `behaviour`: {record: true}, {throw: {message, code}} (a RuntimeException), or null for no callback), then dispatch() of each of `events` (deployed, cancelled, created) within a span. Returns the callbacks' calls ([name, event class, deps]), the first error dispatch() raised, and the span's listener.<name>.<attribute> attributes grouped by listener

mask.reason: where a failure was raised (source file, line, stack) belongs to the runtime: PHP's file and trace, Rust's #[track_caller] location and backtrace

listener.inspect.doc: A listener built as bus.dispatch builds them: getInjections(), and getCallback() (true, or the LogicException a listener without a callback raises)

mask.reason: PHP's message names the listener's class (Tests\Compat\Bus\Clock), Rust's the listener's name: a Rust listener is a value, not a class (see deviations)

deviations.php: The LogicException's message names the listener's class: '<Class> must set a callback via $this->callback()'.
deviations.reason: A Rust listener is a value built with a name, not a class, so the message names it: '<name> must set a callback via callback()'. Masked in listener.inspect; dispatch() catches it on both sides and records the failure on the span.

deviations.php: A callback may throw any \Throwable; error.code, .line, .file and .trace come from it.
deviations.reason: A Rust callback returns a Failure: message and code, plus the file and line where it was raised (#[track_caller]); error.trace is std::backtrace's capture. The locations are masked.
